title: Combining Text (String Concatenation)
body:
Joining Text with the + Operator

In Python, the plus sign + doesn't only add numbers — when used between strings (text), it glues them together end-to-end! This process is called string concatenation.

The Glue Analogy

Imagine words written on paper strips. Using + is like gluing two paper strips together. If you want a space between the words, you must glue a blank space strip " " in between!

Example: String Concatenation
first = "Good"
second = "Morning"

# Without space
print(first + second)          # Displays "GoodMorning"

# With space
print(first + " " + second)    # Displays "Good Morning"

Math Addition vs String Concatenation

Notice how Python decides what to do based on data types from Lesson 2.2 ↗:

Comparison: Numbers vs Strings
# 1. Numbers: Mathematical Addition
print(10 + 20)      # Displays 30

# 2. Strings: Text Concatenation
print("10" + "20")  # Displays 1020

Converting Numbers to Text with str()

You cannot directly concatenate text and an integer: "Level " + 5 causes an error. To join them, convert the integer to a string using str(5): "Level " + str(5) gives "Level 5".
